2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are, inter alia, that the petitioners and the opposite party Nos. 70-71 filed Title Suit No. 05 of 1993 in the 4th Court of the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka for partition of the suit property stating, inter alma, that the suit property originally belonged to Maghu Chowkider and his name was correctly recorded in CS Khatian. Thereafter, Meghu Chowkider died leaving behind two sons, namely-Sheikh Yeasin and Kalimuddin. The property appertaining to schedule Nos. 4 and 5 of the plaint belonged to Sheikh Yeasin. Sheikh Yeasin died in the year 1946 leaving 3 sons, namely-Momtazuddin, Sultan and Magrab Ali, 3 daughters, namely Sharifunnessa, Uttam Nessa and Joytunnessa who possessed the property left by Sheikh Yeasin in ejmali. Thereafter, Momtazuddin died in the year 1968 leaving behind one son, namely Abdul Awal, wife Moti Bibi and 5 daughters Anwara, Fulbanu, Afatunnessa, Sademunnessa and Saleha Khatun. Abdul Awal died in the year 1970 leaving behind mother Moti Bibi, wife Shamsunnahar, 3 sons Montu, Reazuddin and Jashimuddin and 4 daughters Farida, Arjuda, Parul and Kuna. Magrab Ali also died in the year 1962 leaving behind wife Dona Bibi, 3 sons, namely Abdul Matin, Salahuddin and Chand Miah and 4 daughters, namely Nazia Khatun, Razia Khatun, Hamida Khatun and Sufia Khatun. Kalimuddin transferred his share to Salimuddin by way of gift. Salimuddin died in the year 1974 leaving behind wife Talemunnessa, 2 sons, namely Nasir Uddin and Abdul Majid and 7 daughters, namely Akter Banu, Nur Banu, Pari Banu, Angura, Hosne Bibi, Shamsunrkahar, Nurunnahar, Abdul Karim and Abdur Rahim. Thereafter, Abdur Rahim died in the year 1965 leaving behind wife Kadbanu, two sons, namely Zaman Mollah and Hasan Mollah and four daughters, namely Madina, Kulsum, Nazma, Hanufa. Abdul Karim died in the year 1970 leaving behind wife Mabia, and 4 sons, namely Mohsin, Shafiullah, Md. Anis and Md. Yunus. The defendant Nos. 23-45 inherited 11 annas share of Salimuddin. Joytunnssa and the daughter of Yeasin died leaving behind 3 sons, namely Ramizuddin, Rafizuddin, Tafizuddin and 3 daughters, namely Falani, Rahimon, Anna Bibi and Debjan Bibi inherited from Joytunnessa. The defendant Nos. 52-67 are reported to have purchased a portion of the said property and, as such, they have been made as party. The plaintiffs are the successive heirs of the 3 daughters of Sheikh Yeasin and they are entitled to get 1 anna 15 gonda 2 kara 2/3 kranti share from the property. The plaintiffs have been possessing the property by way of ejmali share. The plaintiffs requested the defendants for partition of their shares, but the defendants did not agree with the prayer of the plaintiffs and, as such, they filed the suit for partition of the suit property against the defendants. 

 10. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman (Helal), the learned Advocate with Mr. Mintu Kumar Mondal appearing for the opposite party Nos.73-109 submits that both the Courts below correctly found that Sheikh Yeasin was the predecessor of the plaintiffs and contesting defendants gifted the suit land to his three sons by means of three heba-bil-ewaz deeds and his three daughters got ornaments and cattle heads and, as such, after the sad demise of Sheikh Yeasin, the three daughters did not claim their shares before filing the present suit and therefore, there is no apparent reason to interfere with the concurrent finding of the facts as there is no misreading, non-consideration of evidence and non-interpretation of law critically involved in this case. In this respect, he has referred to the case reported in 15 BLD (AD) 82. He further submits that the opposite party Nos. 73-101 claimed their title through Kalim Uddin and not Sheikh Yeasin and the plaintiffs claimed their portion of land from Sheikh Yeasin and, as such, the suit is decreed and they are entitled to get saham of 0.1323 acre of land since the predecessor of the added opposite parties Abdul Latif was not made party and the observation is required to be given in the judgment. In this connection, the predecessor of the added opposite party Nos. 73-101 became the owners of 0.15 acre of land by way of purchase as well as exchange in the year, 1990-94 and accordingly, separate city survey khatian being No. 5685/1 was duly prepared and published in his name but the plaintiff filed the suit without impleading him as defendant and, as such, the suit is bad for defect of party. 

 14. The Trial Court dismissed the suit holding the view that the suit is not maintainable as the plaintiff did not claim any relief against the impugned three registered heba-bil-ewaz deeds dated 23-11-1945 are genuine and the contentions of the oral gifts are proved. He further held that the oral gifts and the three registered heba-bil-ewaz deeds were acted upon as the latest khatian was prepared in the name of the defendant. The Appellate Court concurred with the judgment and decree of the Trial Court and held that on the basis of the judgment passed in First Appeal No. 156 of 2000, the Trial Court started the trial again and wherein one Momota Rani Chackrovorty was examined as DW-5 who brought the volumes of the registered heba-bil-ewaz deeds and held that the judgment and decree of the Trial Court are based on sound reasoning. In this respect, the relevant portion of the judgment of the Appellate Court may be read as follows: 

 16. The burden of proof to invalidate a document lies upon the plaintiff. Moreover, on the basis of the registered deed, SA and R.S khatians were prepared in the names of the defendants. No two case are similar, every case has to be considered with its own facts and circumstances. The contentions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner is that in the instant case, the Holy Quran and the jainamaz are the consideration against the heba-bil-ewaz but it was not given to the executor of the deeds. The executor of the deeds in his life time did not say anything as to that effect that he was not given consideration i.e. the Holy Quran and the jainamaz. Since the executions of the deeds in question were not disputed, therefore, it is not essential to produce attesting witness. If the execution of a registered deed is denied by the executant then the same may be proved by an attesting witness or by producing the scribe of the deed in question or the person who knows the hand writing of the execution or by comparison of the disputed signatures with the admitted one and thumb impression or by producing thirty years old documents from a proper custody.
